MARRIAGE OF A MINOR — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jane Doe · John Smith

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes the requirements California law imposes before a person under 18 years of age may obtain a marriage license, under Family Code sections 300 through 306 and sections 420 and 423 (Part 1, Validity of Marriage, and Part 3, Solemnization of Marriage, of Division 3 of the Family Code). It covers the general age-18 baseline for consenting to marriage, the court-order and parental- or guardian-consent requirements that apply when one or both parties are under 18, the Family Court Services interview and reporting process the court must follow before ruling on such an order, the 30-day waiting period and its statutory exceptions, the court's discretionary authority to order premarital counseling, the information a minor must be given once an order is issued, and how licensing and solemnization proceed once an order has been granted. It is distinct from this project's Confidential Marriage document, which describes a separate license track under Family Code Part 4 (commencing with Section 500) available to adults living together as spouses, and from this project's Common Law Marriage document, which addresses California's non-recognition of marriage formed by cohabitation and consent alone rather than the minor-specific consent and court-order requirements addressed here. This document is for parties named Jane Doe and John Smith. This document is informational only. It states what the statutes require; it does not determine whether any specific minor, parent, guardian, or court will grant, deny, or condition a particular request for permission to marry, and it is not a substitute for legal advice about a specific person's situation. Only a court, applying these statutes to the actual facts before it, can determine whether a particular minor may be issued a marriage license.

THE GENERAL RULE FOR PERSONS 18 OR OLDER — FAMILY CODE SECTION 301
Family Code section 301 states the general baseline: two unmarried persons who are 18 years of age or older, and who are not otherwise disqualified from marrying, are capable of consenting to and consummating a marriage without any court order or parental consent. The court-order and consent requirements described in the rest of this document apply only when at least one party to the intended marriage is under 18.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Two unmarried persons 18 years of age or older, who are not otherwise disqualified, are capable of consenting to and consummating marriage."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 301, Cal. Fam. Code § 301 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=301.)
  Known gap: This clause states only the age-18 baseline in section 301 itself. It does not address what "not otherwise disqualified" means -- for example, the separate statutory rules on incestuous or bigamous marriages found elsewhere in the Family Code -- because that is a distinct topic from the minor-specific consent and court-order requirements this document addresses.

THE COURT-ORDER REQUIREMENT FOR A PERSON UNDER 18 — FAMILY CODE SECTION 302
Family Code section 302 provides the general rule for a minor with at least one parent or guardian able to consent: an unmarried person under 18 years of age may be issued a marriage license only upon obtaining a court order granting permission to marry, following the procedure Family Code section 304 describes. The court order itself is not the last step -- section 302(b) also requires that the court order and the written consent of at least one parent or the guardian of each underage party be filed with the clerk of the court, and that a certified copy of the order be presented to the county clerk at the time the marriage license is issued.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "An unmarried person under 18 years of age may be issued a marriage license upon obtaining a court order granting permission to the underage person or persons to marry, in accordance with the requirements described in Section 304."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 302, Cal. Fam. Code § 302(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=302.)
  "The court order and written consent of at least one of the parents or the guardian of each underage person shall be filed with the clerk of the court, and a certified copy of the order shall be presented to the county clerk at the time the marriage license is issued."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 302, Cal. Fam. Code § 302(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=302.)
  Known gap: This clause addresses only the case where the minor has a parent or guardian available and able to consent. It does not address the different pathway under Family Code section 303 for a minor who has no parent, or no parent capable of consenting, which is addressed in a separate clause of this document. It also does not independently verify the county clerk's own administrative procedures for accepting the certified copy of the order, which are not stated in section 302 itself.

WHEN A MINOR HAS NO PARENT ABLE TO CONSENT — FAMILY CODE SECTION 303
Family Code section 303 addresses the situation where the minor has no parent, or no parent capable of giving consent. If it appears to the court's satisfaction, on the minor's own application, that the minor requires a written consent to marry and has no parent or no parent capable of consenting, the court itself may make an order consenting to the issuance of a marriage license and granting the minor permission to marry, following the same section 304 procedure that applies to an order under section 302. As under section 302, the order must be filed with the clerk of the court and a certified copy presented to the county clerk when the marriage license is issued.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "If it appears to the satisfaction of the court by application of a minor that the minor requires a written consent to marry and that the minor has no parent or has no parent capable of consenting, the court may make an order consenting to the issuance of a marriage license and granting permission to the minor to marry, in accordance with the requirements described in Section 304."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 303, Cal. Fam. Code § 303 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=303.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes section 303 as currently written. It does not independently verify how a court determines that a parent is "not capable of consenting" in practice, or what evidence a minor's application under this section must contain beyond the statute's own general standard, because section 303 does not itself define those terms further.

THE FAMILY COURT SERVICES INTERVIEW AND REPORT — FAMILY CODE SECTION 304(A)
Before a court may issue an order granting permission to marry under section 302 or 303, Family Code section 304(a) requires it to take several specific steps. The court must require Family Court Services to separately interview the parties intending to marry and, if applicable, at least one parent or the guardian of each party who is a minor -- and if more than one parent or guardian is interviewed, they must be interviewed separately from one another. Family Court Services must then prepare and submit to the court a written report assessing any potential force, threat, persuasion, fraud, coercion, or duress by either party or their family members relating to the intended marriage, along with a recommendation on whether to grant or deny permission to marry; if Family Court Services knows or reasonably suspects either party is a victim of child abuse or neglect, it must also report that to the county child protective services agency. After receiving that report, the court must separately interview each party in camera before making its final determination, and must consider whether there is evidence of coercion or undue influence on the minor.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Require Family Court Services to separately interview the parties intending to marry and, if applicable, at least one of the parents or the guardian of each party who is a minor."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(a)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  "Require Family Court Services to prepare and submit to the court a written report, containing any assessment of potential force, threat, persuasion, fraud, coercion, or duress by either of the parties or their family members relating to the intended marriage."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(a)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  "Consider whether there is evidence of coercion or undue influence on the minor."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(a)(3)-(4) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  Known gap: This clause describes the statutory steps a court must take before ruling; it does not describe how a specific Family Court Services office schedules or conducts these interviews in practice, nor what its written report format looks like, because section 304(a) leaves those operational details to the court and to Family Court Services rather than specifying them in the statute itself.

THE 30-DAY WAITING PERIOD BEFORE A LICENSE MAY BE REQUESTED — FAMILY CODE SECTION 304(B)
Family Code section 304(b) imposes a waiting period after a court order is issued, in the specific circumstance where one or both of the parties are 17 years of age or younger: the parties become eligible to request a marriage license no earlier than 30 days from the time the court order was issued. This waiting period is separate from, and additional to, the underlying requirement to obtain the court order itself.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "if one or both of the parties are 17 years of age or younger, the parties shall be eligible to request a marriage license no earlier than 30 days from the time the court order was issued"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  Known gap: This clause states the 30-day rule as section 304(b) itself frames it, keyed to a party being 17 or younger rather than to every case involving a minor. It does not address the statutory exceptions to this specific 30-day requirement, which are addressed in a separate clause of this document covering section 304(f).

THE COURT'S DISCRETIONARY AUTHORITY TO ORDER PREMARITAL COUNSELING — FAMILY CODE SECTION 304(C)
As part of a court order granting permission to marry under section 302 or 303, Family Code section 304(c) gives the court discretionary authority -- not a mandatory duty -- to require the parties to a prospective minor's marriage to participate in premarital counseling concerning the social, economic, and personal responsibilities that come with marriage, if the court considers it necessary. The statute specifically provides that the parties cannot be required to confer with counselors provided by religious organizations of any denomination. In deciding whether to order counseling, the court must consider, among other factors, the parties' ability to pay for it, and the court may impose a reasonable fee to cover the cost of counseling provided by the county or the court, which must be used exclusively for that purpose.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "the court shall, if it considers it necessary, require the parties to the prospective marriage of a minor to participate in premarital counseling concerning social, economic, and personal responsibilities incident to marriage. The parties shall not be required to confer with counselors provided by religious organizations of any denomination."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  Known gap: This clause describes the court's authority and the constraints the statute places on it; it does not identify which counseling providers a given county actually makes available, or what a reasonable fee amount looks like in practice, because section 304(c) leaves those specifics to the counseling provider and the court's own fee-setting rather than fixing them in the statute.

WHAT THE COURT ORDER ITSELF MUST DOCUMENT — FAMILY CODE SECTION 304(D)
Family Code section 304(d) specifies information the court order granting permission to marry must document. Only for purposes of completing the document described in Health and Safety Code section 102233, and not for purposes of deciding the underlying request, the gender of each party intending to marry, if provided, must be documented on the order. The date of birth of each party intending to marry must also be documented on the order. In addition, so the person solemnizing the marriage can meet the requirement in Family Code section 423(b) and the local registrar can meet the requirement in Health and Safety Code section 102356(a), the court must provide the parties who are granted permission to marry with a copy of the order itself.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "the gender of each party intending to marry, if provided, shall be documented on the court order granting permission to marry"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(d)(1)-(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  "the court shall provide parties who are granted permission to marry with a copy of the court order granting permission to marry"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(d)(3) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  Known gap: This clause quotes section 304(d)'s own text describing what must appear on the order and to whom a copy must go. It does not independently verify the text of Health and Safety Code sections 102233 or 102356, which section 304(d) cross-references but which were not fetched or reviewed in preparing this document.

INFORMATION THE MINOR MUST BE GIVEN WHEN AN ORDER ISSUES — FAMILY CODE SECTION 304(E)
Family Code section 304(e) requires that, upon issuance of the order granting permission to marry, the minor be provided with several categories of information: the rights and responsibilities of an emancipated minor, including the effects of emancipation described in the Family Code's emancipation chapter beginning at section 7050; the circumstances under which a marriage may be judicially determined void or voidable and adjudged a nullity, and the procedure for obtaining that determination; the procedures for legal separation or dissolution of marriage; telephone numbers for the National Domestic Violence Hotline and the National Sexual Assault Hotline; and the conditions under which an unemancipated minor may leave home and remain in a shelter or otherwise live separately from a parent or guardian, whether a parent's or guardian's consent or acquiescence is required for that, the minor's rights to seek a protective or restraining order to prevent abuse, and the minor's rights to enter into contracts, including contracts for legal services and mental health counseling.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Upon issuance of the order granting permission to marry, the minor shall be provided with the following information:"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  "Telephone numbers for the National Domestic Violence Hotline and the National Sexual Assault Hotline."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(e)(3) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  Known gap: This clause lists the categories of information section 304(e) requires be given to the minor; it does not itself reproduce that underlying substantive information (for example, the actual emancipation rights under Family Code section 7050 et seq., or the actual nullity grounds), which this project's own separate Emancipation of a Minor and Nullity of Marriage documents address in more depth. It also does not verify who is responsible for actually delivering this information to the minor in practice, since section 304(e) states that it "shall be provided" without naming the specific person or office who provides it.

EXCEPTIONS TO THE INTERVIEW/REPORT PROCESS AND THE 30-DAY WAIT — FAMILY CODE SECTION 304(F)
Family Code section 304(f) creates two distinct, narrower exceptions. First, subdivisions (a) and (b) -- the Family Court Services interview-and-report process and the 30-day waiting period -- do not apply to a minor who is 17 years of age and who has achieved a high school diploma or a high school equivalency certificate. Second, and separately, subdivision (b) alone -- only the 30-day waiting period -- does not apply to a minor who is 16 or 17 years of age and who is pregnant, or whose prospective spouse is pregnant; that narrower pregnancy exception does not excuse the party from the Family Court Services interview-and-report process, only from the 30-day wait.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Subdivisions (a) and (b) do not apply to a minor who is 17 years of age and who has achieved a high school diploma or a high school equivalency certificate."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(f)(1) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  "Subdivision (b) does not apply to a minor who is 16 or 17 years of age and who is pregnant or whose prospective spouse is pregnant."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 304, Cal. Fam. Code § 304(f)(2) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=304.)
  Known gap: This clause states the two exceptions exactly as section 304(f) draws them; note that they are not interchangeable -- the diploma/equivalency exception in paragraph (1) reaches both subdivisions (a) and (b), while the pregnancy exception in paragraph (2) reaches only subdivision (b). This clause does not address how a minor or the court verifies a high school equivalency certificate or a pregnancy for these purposes, because section 304(f) does not itself specify a verification procedure.

LICENSING, SOLEMNIZATION, AND RETURNING THE LICENSE AFTER AN ORDER ISSUES — FAMILY CODE SECTIONS 306, 420, AND 423
Once a court order granting permission to marry has been obtained, the marriage still must go through California's general licensing and solemnization process. Family Code section 306 states that, with an exception not relevant here, a marriage must be licensed, solemnized, and authenticated, and the authenticated license returned to the county recorder of the county where it was issued; noncompliance with these requirements by a nonparty to the marriage does not itself invalidate the marriage. Family Code section 420(a) states that no particular form of ceremony is required for solemnization, but the parties must declare, in the physical presence of the person solemnizing the marriage and necessary witnesses, that they take each other as spouses. Finally, Family Code section 423(b) adds a minor-specific requirement at the return-of-license stage: the person solemnizing the marriage must include with the returned marriage license a copy of the section 304 court order granting permission to marry, if one or both of the parties were minors at the time of solemnization.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "a marriage shall be licensed, solemnized, and authenticated, and the authenticated marriage license shall be returned to the county recorder of the county where the marriage license was issued, as provided in this part"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 306, Cal. Fam. Code § 306 (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=306.)
  "No particular form for the ceremony of marriage is required for solemnization of the marriage, but the parties shall declare, in the physical presence of the person solemnizing the marriage and necessary witnesses, that they take each other as spouses."
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 420, Cal. Fam. Code § 420(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=420.)
  "the person solemnizing the marriage shall include with the marriage license described in subdivision (a) a copy of the court order granting permission to marry described in Section 304, if one or both of the parties to the marriage were minors at the time of solemnization of the marriage"
  — Cal. Fam. Code § 423, Cal. Fam. Code § 423(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=FAM&sectionNum=423.)
  Known gap: This clause does not independently verify Family Code section 307 (the exception section 306 itself cross-references), section 422 (the endorsement requirement section 423(a) cross-references), or the identity of who is authorized to solemnize a marriage in California, all of which are governed by other Family Code sections not fetched for this document. It also does not address the separate confidential-marriage license track under Part 4 of this division, which this project's Confidential Marriage document covers.

SIGNATURES AND ACKNOWLEDGMENT
The undersigned acknowledge that they have read and reviewed this information sheet regarding the California statutory requirements for a marriage involving a party under 18 years of age. Minor party: Jane Doe, date of birth January 1, 2009. Other party: John Smith. Anticipated marriage date: June 1, 2026. County: Los Angeles County. Court and case number, if a request for a court order granting permission to marry has been filed: Superior Court of California, County of Los Angeles, case number 24FL012345. Consenting parent or guardian (if applicable): Jane Doe. The undersigned acknowledge that this document is informational only, that it does not constitute legal advice, and that it does not itself grant, deny, or affect any court order, marriage license, or right to marry -- only a court and, where applicable, the county clerk, can do that.

First, subdivisions (a) and (b) -- the Family Court Services interview-and-report process and the 30-day waiting period -- do not apply to a minor who is 17 years of age and who has achieved a high school diploma or a high school equivalency certificate. Second, and separately, subdivision (b) alone -- only the 30-day waiting period -- does not apply to a minor who is 16 or 17 years of age and who is pregnant, or whose prospective spouse is pregnant; that narrower pregnancy exception does not excuse the party from the Family Court Services interview-and-report process, only from the 30-day wait.

Subdivision (b) does not apply to a minor who is 16 or 17 years of age and who is pregnant or whose prospective spouse is pregnant.

expectedJSON.gap: This clause states the two exceptions exactly as section 304(f) draws them; note that they are not interchangeable -- the diploma/equivalency exception in paragraph (1) reaches both subdivisions (a) and (b), while the pregnancy exception in paragraph (2) reaches only subdivision (b). This clause does not address how a minor or the court verifies a high school equivalency certificate or a pregnancy for these purposes, because section 304(f) does not itself specify a verification procedure.

expectedJSON.body: Once a court order granting permission to marry has been obtained, the marriage still must go through California's general licensing and solemnization process. Family Code section 306 states that, with an exception not relevant here, a marriage must be licensed, solemnized, and authenticated, and the authenticated license returned to the county recorder of the county where it was issued; noncompliance with these requirements by a nonparty to the marriage does not itself invalidate the marriage. Family Code section 420(a) states that no particular form of ceremony is required for solemnization, but the parties must declare, in the physical presence of the person solemnizing the marriage and necessary witnesses, that they take each other as spouses. Finally, Family Code section 423(b) adds a minor-specific requirement at the return-of-license stage: the person solemnizing the marriage must include with the returned marriage license a copy of the section 304 court order granting permission to marry, if one or both of the parties were minors at the time of solemnization.
